- Model tends to overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early or too high following a sharp price increase, then underestimates the subsequent correction.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model fails to anticipate gradual pullback after peaks.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher values, especially in the 2nd–3rd forecast days after a spike.
- Forecast horizon 1–3 days: model consistently overestimates; horizon 4–7: underestimates, suggesting asymmetric error structure.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent price drops — fails to adjust downward in time.
- Overshoot after spikes is common, followed by a lagged correction that model misses.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to reset expectations after a sharp move, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the 2nd half of the 30-day window, suggesting model underestimates tail risk or volatility clustering.
